I have a SNES, Sega Genesis, 360 and PC.

As another commenter said, it's kind of hard to recommend something when we don't know what systems you have. That being said, Tales of Symphonia is my absolute favorite game of all time. VERY close seconds are the Metroid series, the Mega Man Battle Network games, Zelda, Final Fantasy Tactics and it's sequels...I could go on.

I'll list a few, for the sake of recommendation.

  • Mark of the Ninja

A stealth platformer from the developers of Don't Starve and Invisible Inc. The gameplay is near perfect, the art style looks phenomenal in motion, and the voice acting makes it so fun to scare the guards. Bring a controller if you're on PC, but this one is highly recommended.

  • Deus Ex

Right about now, roughly half of Voat is reinstalling this game because I mentioned it. Yep, it's one of those games.

A futuristic FPSRPG in which you play as JC Denton, a nanoaugmented agent working for UNATCO (United Nations Anti-Terrorist Coalition). Any build that isn't specced in Swimming and Poison Resistance can work, and you can choose how to play to fit your playstyle. More importantly, in one of my favorite design decisions, the game allows for player actions to affect the story, but doesn't telegraph which actions will.

It's a bit old, so you'll need to use a few mods if you get it running. You'll probably want the DirectX 10 renderer and Deus Exe from kentie.net. Leave GUI scaling off, turning it on makes the GUI shrink to unreadable size, as well as the sniper scope and binocular graphic.

  • Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater

I can't think of anything major that's wrong with this game. It has that Metal Gear problem where one terrible line of dialog will occasionally ruin an otherwise perfect and emotional scene, but it's still one of the best games I've ever played. There's mechanical depth everywhere; if you think it'll work, it'll probably work.

The story is absolutely fantastic, with (mostly) great voice acting and a lot of fun moments. Despite being the third in a notoriously convoluted series, you don't need to have played the earlier games to understand what's going on. It also has one of my favorite female characters in any video game, The Boss. And that ending, oh boy that ending. Watching a shitty compressed YouTube video of it still gives me chills. Highly, highly recommended.

New NBC Poll: Trump still leads. Cruz, Fironia, and Carson see gains. Bush and Walker tied for 5th

first, the polling methodology here is similar to YouGov, though no track record to speak of. it's reasonable to think that these might be solid results but time will tell if this polling alliance produces consistently accurate results.

next, the top line of this poll - that Trump is still leading the Republican primary field and that a shake up occurred below him - has already been discussed at length.

a point i haven't seen discussed much anywhere is that while Trump received good marks for best preformance in the debate (18%, second to Carly Fiorina), he also scored very high on "who do you think did the worst job in the Republican debates?" 29% said Trump; next highest was Rand Paul at 14%, then 'none of them' at 13%. what this means, i think, is sort of obvious (but it's nice to have empirical evidence): Trump is polarizing. as many people that love him, hate him - even within the Republican primary electorate. so it makes sense that he's got significant support, and that he leads a large field; so long as the "anyone but Trump" portion of the electorate is split between a lot of other candidates, Trump can be in the lead. he will probably never consolidate ALL the Republicans, though, because a significant portion of them have very negative feelings about him.

finally, a really interesting thing even the release doesn't point out... if you look at the top of page 3 and the bottom of page 5, you'll see tables showing the four poll results this alliance has so far. page 3 has party ID and page 5 has ideology. both party ID questions show movement toward the Republican Party and away from the Democratic Party; those on page 5, toward conservative and away from liberal. importantly, this DOESN'T necessarily mean individual people are changing from one party to another; polls are susceptible to different people being engaged enough to talk to them. it DOES mean, though - assuming the polls are reliable - that Republican identifiers are getting more excited, becoming a larger proportion of the electorate. why? this poll doesn't address that.
